formula_reading_notes.alpha_branch: Eq. (17) as printed labels 0.249(M2/M1)^0.56 + 0.0035(M2/M1)^1.5 'M1 >= M2' and 0.088(M2/M1)^-0.15 + 0.165(M2/M1) 'M1 <= M2'. The paper's own worked example (He -> Au, M2/M1 = 48.75, i.e. M1 < M2) and Fig. 1 use the 0.249 branch for M2/M1 > 1, so the labels as printed are inconsistent with the paper's use. The builder uses the branch the paper itself uses (0.249 branch for M1 <= M2); the two branches agree at M2/M1 = 1 (0.2525 vs 0.253). Only O+ / N+ on C (M1 > M2) is affected.
formula_reading_notes.threshold: Eq. (18): Eth/Us = 6.7/gamma for M1 >= M2 and (1 + 5.7 M1/M2)/gamma for M1 <= M2 (labels consistent with the worked example).
formula_reading_notes.W_inconsistency: Table 1 W equals the caption factor times the Table 1 Us for Fe (0.28*4.28), Ni (0.30*4.44) and W (0.24*8.9), but not for Mo (Table 1 W = 2.39 = 0.35*6.82, caption 'W = 0.45Us'). For best-fit-Us combinations it is also not stated whether k multiplies the Table 1 or the fitted Us. The builder evaluates all three readings (Table 1 W; k * Table 1 Us; k * fitted Us) and reports the spread.
formula_reading_notes.worked_example: the printed example mixes 195.1 and 197 for the Au mass and prints gamma = 0.07878 (our arithmetic with its own masses gives 0.0781); the builder accepts a 2 % tolerance on the yield and records the residual
